title: Kira Goldberg Departs Netflix for Paramount as Jesse Ehrman Earns Promotion – Deadline News
body:
Kira Goldberg, a veteran executive who has helped shape Netflix’s film slate for the past eight years, is exiting the streaming giant to assume the role of President of the Motion Picture Group at Paramount Pictures. She will join forces with longtime colleague Don Granger, who was recently elevated to head Paramount’s film division. At the same time, Warner Bros. Discovery announced the promotion of Jesse Ehrman, who will now oversee the studio’s drama, holiday, thriller and family‑oriented projects.

Goldberg’s departure marks the end of a tenure that saw Netflix transition from a modest content buyer to a dominant global studio. Starting as a development executive in 2015, she rose through the ranks to oversee the company’s drama, holiday, thriller and family portfolios, shepherding titles such as “The Power of the Dog,” “Murder Mystery 2,” and the family‑focused “The Christmas Chronicles” franchise. Under her guidance, Netflix’s original film output not only grew in volume but also garnered critical acclaim, earning multiple Oscar nominations and wins. Her move to Paramount comes at a pivotal moment for the traditional studio, which is seeking to rebuild its theatrical pipeline after a pandemic‑induced slump.

Paramount’s decision to bring Goldberg on board signals a strategic push to blend streaming sensibilities with classic theatrical releases. The studio, which has been navigating a complex landscape of hybrid distribution models, hopes Goldberg’s expertise in genre‑spanning content will revitalize its slate and attract diverse audiences. Partnering her with Don Granger—who previously led Paramount’s acquisition and development efforts—creates a leadership duo that blends deep industry relationships with a data‑driven approach honed at Netflix. Industry observers note that Goldberg’s track record of leveraging audience analytics to green‑light projects could help Paramount better predict box‑office performance while still nurturing prestige‑film ambitions.

The promotion of Jesse Ehrman at Warner Bros. Discovery underscores a broader trend of studios consolidating leadership to streamline decision‑making across overlapping genres. Ehrman, who previously served as senior vice president of drama, will now oversee a broader portfolio that includes holiday and family titles—areas where Netflix has excelled under Goldberg’s watch. Warner’s move reflects an acknowledgement that genre‑specific expertise is increasingly valuable in a market where streaming platforms dominate the family and holiday segments, while theatrical releases remain the primary revenue driver for dramas and thrillers.

Goldberg’s transition also highlights the fluidity of talent between streaming services and legacy studios. As the lines between “digital” and “traditional” content production blur, executives with cross‑platform experience are in high demand. Netflix’s willingness to lose a key figure suggests confidence in its deep bench, while Paramount’s recruitment demonstrates a willingness to import proven streaming expertise to reinvigorate its theatrical brand. The industry is likely to see more such migrations as studios seek to balance the immediacy of streaming with the cultural cachet of cinema.

Looking ahead, Goldberg’s impact at Paramount will be measured by the studio’s ability to deliver a slate that resonates both on the big screen and on streaming platforms. Early projects under her stewardship are expected to include a mix of high‑concept thrillers, family‑friendly adventures, and holiday‑season offerings—genres where she has consistently delivered both commercial success and critical recognition. If successful, her appointment could serve as a blueprint for other studios aiming to bridge the gap between data‑driven streaming strategies and the timeless appeal of theatrical storytelling, shaping the next chapter of Hollywood’s evolving distribution landscape.
